title: Joint BUN–creatinine interaction fails to improve serum urate prediction in an independent NHANES cycle
abstract: We tested whether joint information in routine renal chemistry adds to standard-measure representations of concurrent serum urate. Models were fit in 5,231 NHANES 2007–08 adults and frozen before evaluation in a separate 2009–10 probability sample. In 5,628 NHANES 2009–10 adults, a frozen log-BUN×log-creatinine interaction did not improve serum urate prediction beyond nonlinear components, their ratio, eGFR and demographics: weighted MSE difference (baseline minus augmented) -0.001483 (mg/dL)^2, approximate 95% interval -0.015930 to 0.001558. Added predictive value is not established. Cubic marginals, additional biochemical adjustment, unweighted fitting and restricted kidney-function subsets did not rescue the point estimate. This existing-data negative result does not establish equivalence or clinical utility.
